vector: SEATS - the per-year PERSON join. One row per driver per season, binding a DRIVER (by driverId) to a TEAM for THIS season. Plus the team register the whole app colours from. This is the person-axis twin of the weekend vector: identity is timeless, the season binding is a join.
why_a_seat_and_not_a_driver: A driver's TEAM is a per-year fact, not identity - Sergio Perez drives for Cadillac in 2026 and did not before, and mid-season moves happen. So the joining row is a SEAT (driver x team x season), exactly the shape circuit x weekend takes on the place axis. A timeless DRIVER table (name, nationality, career) is deliberately NOT built yet: there is one season of data, and a cross-season identity file holding a single season is a table waiting for a reason. Split this into DRIVER + SEAT the day a 2025 store exists. Decision Log J10.
docs: ../../README.md (Data Model) + the F1 Racetracks App Decision Log, J10 and J13.
canonical_for: DISPLAY - the driver's short name and the team colour. Every consumer resolves those from here.
not_canonical_for: WHAT HAPPENED. The `driver` and `team` strings on each classification row STAY, and stay authoritative for that round. They are the historical record of who drove for whom on that day, they keep a round file readable on its own, and they survive a mid-season team change that this file's single row per season cannot express. This file is a projection for rendering, never a replacement for the result.
unsourced_fields: Three-letter `code` and car `number` are NOT in this file. They are not present anywhere in the store and were not sourced in this pass. Per the canon rule: sourced or absent. Add them from official sources, never from memory.
colour_provenance_2026_08_01: The four colours that were null until now (Aston Martin, Audi, Haas, Cadillac) were NOT invented for this file. They are the values `source/standings/base.css` and `source/weekend/base.css` already declare as --t-astonmartin / --t-audi / --t-haas / --t-cadillac, which are themselves the native palettes in shared/themes/f1/ brought to display lightness: audi = audi.json `accent`, cadillac = cadillac.json `accent`, aston-martin = aston-martin.json `accent`, haas = haas.json `accent-2` lifted off a light-mode palette onto a dark board. Two of four surfaces have rendered these all along; only the circuit guide fell back to grey, because it resolves colour from here and the other two resolve from CSS. Re-deriving from the palettes would have produced a FIFTH set of team colours.
colour_format_note: Four rows carry oklch() and seven carry hex, on purpose. The oklch values are copied VERBATIM from the stylesheets - converting them to hex would mean doing colour math by hand, and a wrong digit in a colour literal is invisible in review. Mixed format is the cheaper honest cost. oklch() is valid CSS in every browser this app targets, and teamColor() returns the string untouched.
known_adjacencies: ⚠️ AUDI sits 7 hue degrees from FERRARI at identical lightness (0.60 0.17 20 vs 0.60 0.21 27). Tight, and named rather than hidden. audi.json's other identity token is titanium (0.78 0.006 250), which would separate them completely - NOT taken, because Haas is already near-neutral steel and the unresolved fallback is a light grey, so titanium would put three greys on one board. Red beside red is the lesser problem. ⚠️ ASTON MARTIN (hue 168) sits 10 degrees from MERCEDES (178); aston-martin.json's `accent-2` lime, oklch(0.86 0.19 130), is the one-line swap if it reads too close on a phone. Both reversals are a single value.
⚠️_two_colour_tables: THIS REGISTER IS NOT THE ONLY TEAM-COLOUR SOURCE, and the two disagree. `source/standings/base.css` and `source/weekend/base.css` each declare a full --t-<team> set (duplicated a third time inside story-mode-reference.html). They differ from the hexes below for EVERY team, and on Alpine they differ in kind: this file says #7DE3FF (cyan), the stylesheets say oklch(0.70 0.14 344) (pink). Alpine renders a different colour depending on which screen you are on. The duplication is structural rather than lazy - CSS cannot read a JSON file at parse time, so unifying means injecting custom properties at boot from this register. That is an aesthetic change to seven teams and it is Michael's call, not a cleanup. Decision Log J13.

teams.color_note: ⚠️ CONFLICT: the stylesheets render Alpine PINK, oklch(0.70 0.14 344). This cyan and that pink are both live, on different screens. Unresolved on purpose - see the two-colour-tables note above.

teams.color_source: --t-astonmartin, from aston-martin.json `accent` oklch(0.52 0.10 175). British racing green. RESOLVED 2026-08-01. The old module-09 map held #66D1A7 under the dead keys `AstonMartin`/`Aston` and never once rendered; that value was not adopted, because it was a mint at ~hue 160 that sat even closer to Mercedes than this does.
--t-audi, from audi.json `accent` oklch(0.57 0.21 25). Audi red. RESOLVED 2026-08-01. See known_adjacencies: this is the tight one against Ferrari, and titanium was considered and refused.

--t-haas, from haas.json `accent-2` oklch(0.30 0.015 260) - the steel secondary, lifted from a light-mode palette to a dark board. RESOLVED 2026-08-01. haas.json's `accent` is red and would have been a third red; its surfaces are white and would have read as emphasised text rather than a team.

--t-cadillac, from cadillac.json `accent` oklch(0.78 0.13 85). Gold on navy chrome, the 2026 entrant's identity. RESOLVED 2026-08-01. Hue 92 against McLaren's orange 56 is a comfortable gap; gold and orange separate on chroma as well.

team_colour_rule: Team colours are a LOCAL IDENTITY LAYER, not a theme vector - they ride on top of whatever theme is applied and are never swept into one. An unresolved colour falls back to the neutral tone AND logs a warning; it never fails silently. As of 2026-08-01 all eleven resolve, so that warning firing means a NEW team has appeared in the data and nobody added it here.
provenance: All 22 driverId / driver / team triples read directly from f1-results/2026/r09-silverstone.json at commit a191700, which is the one round file carrying every driver on the grid in a single classification (22 rows: 20 classified, 2 DNF). `short` is the last whitespace-delimited token of `driver` - the same transform module 09 was computing at render time, moved to data so it stops being derived from a display string. The four colours added 2026-08-01 are copied verbatim from the stylesheets named above. Nothing in this file was typed from memory.
